answer: One workable design: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because yarrow only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, harbor is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any knoll approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
